title: How to show the path bar in Finder on Mac: quick steps for recent macOS
metaTitle: How to show the path bar in Finder on Mac, step by step
description: Learn how to show the path bar in Finder on Mac using View > Show Path Bar, the ⌥⌘P shortcut, or a quick Option-key peek at the bottom edge.
targetKeyword: how to show the path bar in finder on mac
intro: To show the path bar in Finder on Mac, open a Finder window and choose View > Show Path Bar from the menu bar. The path bar then appears near the bottom of the window and lists the folders that contain the file or folder you have selected.
tldr: Open a Finder window, then choose View > Show Path Bar from the menu bar at the top of the screen.
The path bar sits at the bottom of the window and lists the folders that hold the current item.
Hold the Option (⌥) key to show the path bar briefly, as Apple describes it.
Third-party guides give ⌥⌘P as a toggle shortcut. Apple's Mac Help page does not list one.
Choose View > Show Path Bar again to hide it.

stats.label: Release date of macOS 27 Golden Gate, the version Apple's Mac Help page lists first
Later macOS 27 point release, build 26B123, released October 26, 2026

blocks.text: Finder is the file browser built into every Mac. The path bar is a thin strip at the bottom of a Finder window. It shows where you are, one folder at a time. It is off by default, so most people never see it. Turning it on takes about a minute and needs nothing extra installed.
The menu route: View > Show Path Bar

Start with the menu bar at the top of the screen. Click the Finder window so it is the active window. Then open the View menu and choose Show Path Bar. The strip appears at the bottom edge of that window. iDownloadBlog reports that the bar shows in all Finder windows, in any view mode.

Apple's Mac Help page describes the bar as showing the location and the nested folders that contain the file or folder you pick. That is the whole job of the bar. It answers the question where am I, with each folder spelled out. If you saved a file and lost it, this strip shows you the folder chain it sits in.

Selection matters. Another user in the same Apple Community thread says the bar appears at the bottom only when a Favorites folder or a specific item is selected. Apple's page does not confirm that. If the bar seems missing, click a folder in the sidebar or a file in the window, then check the View menu again.
Use the path bar to move around

The bar is more than a label. You can click it. Click any folder in the bar and Finder shows that folder's subfolders in the window. This can be quicker than double-clicking your way back through several levels, especially deep inside a project folder.

items: Click a folder in the path bar to show its subfolders in the window.
Control-click a folder in the path bar to copy its pathname.
Read each name as a folder that holds the next name in the chain.
Leave the bar on while you learn a new folder layout.

blocks.text: Copied pathnames are useful outside Finder. You can paste one into a Terminal command, a support ticket, or a note that needs an exact location. Copy the path once, then paste it where you need it. Retyping a long folder chain invites mistakes.
Hide it again, or toggle with ⌥⌘P

To hide the bar, open View and choose Show Path Bar again. Mainspring describes this toggle behavior. Third-party guides from iDownloadBlog and Mainspring also name ⌥⌘P as a shortcut that toggles the bar. Apple's Mac Help page does not list that shortcut. Treat it as a third-party tip, and check the View menu if the shortcut does nothing.
Compare the four ways to show the path bar

rows: Turns the bar on, or off when chosen again
defaults write com.apple.finder ShowPathbar -bool true, then killall Finder
Turns the bar on from Terminal
blocks.caption: Four ways to show the path bar, and where each one is documented.

blocks.text: Use the menu route first. It is the one Apple documents. The shortcut is the fastest once you have it memorized. The Terminal method is the least documented option, and the Terminal section below explains why.
Peek at the path bar with the Option key

Apple's Mac Help page says you can press the Option key to show the path bar momentarily. Use this when you only need to check a location. Hold ⌥, look at the bottom of the window, then let go. Apple describes the display as momentary, so do not expect the bar to stay on.
Show the status bar too

The status bar is a separate strip. Choose View > Show Status Bar, or press ⌘/, to turn it on. Mainspring says it sits under the path bar. When the path bar is off, the status bar moves to the bottom of the window. Turn on both if you want location and context at the same time.
The Terminal method, and why to wait

Some guides give a Terminal command: defaults write com.apple.finder ShowPathbar -bool true, followed by killall Finder. macos-defaults.com lists it. The default value there is false, which means hidden. The page lists Sonoma, Ventura, Monterey, and Big Sur. It does not list Tahoe or macOS 27, so the result on those versions is not verified.

The killall Finder step restarts Finder. Save any open work before you run it. Command names are easy to mistype, so copy them exactly, including the capital P in ShowPathbar. If the menu route works, you do not need Terminal at all.
Common mistakes with the path bar

items: Looking in the Finder menu. The option lives under View in the menu bar.
Expecting the bar with nothing selected. Select a folder or file first.
Mixing up the path bar and the status bar. The path bar is View > Show Path Bar. The status bar is View > Show Status Bar, or ⌘/.
Holding Command when you meant Option. ⌥ alone peeks. ⌥⌘P toggles.
Trusting an old guide without checking the menu. The iDownloadBlog article dates from 2015, with a 2026 update note.
Reaching for Terminal first. The menu route is documented and needs no commands.

blocks.text: Check your macOS version first

Apple's Mac Help page has a version selector. It lists macOS 27 Golden Gate first, followed by macOS Tahoe 26 and older. The steps on the page do not name one version. To find your version, open the Apple menu and choose About This Mac.

macOS 27 Golden Gate was released on September 14, 2026, according to Wikipedia. Version 27.2, build 26B123, followed on October 26, 2026. Wikipedia describes no Finder or path bar changes in that release. Your menu should match the steps here. If it does not, follow what your screen shows and check Apple's page for your version.
What to do next

Once the bar is on, use it as a map. When you lose track of where a file sits, click up the path until you reach the folder you want. Control-click a folder to copy its path for a support ticket or a Terminal command. Leave the bar on for a week and see how often you actually use it.

Some details on this page come from third-party guides and forum replies. Apple's Mac Help page is the base for the menu steps. Where a claim comes from a forum or a blog, the text says so. If your Mac shows a different label, trust the label on your screen.

faq.question: Where is the path bar in Finder on Mac?
faq.answer: It sits near the bottom of the Finder window. Apple's Mac Help page says it shows the location and the nested folders that contain the file or folder you selected. Turn it on with View > Show Path Bar.

faq.question: What is the keyboard shortcut to show the path bar?
faq.answer: Third-party guides from iDownloadBlog and Mainspring give ⌥⌘P as a toggle. Apple's Mac Help page does not list a shortcut. If the shortcut does nothing, use View > Show Path Bar instead.

faq.question: Why don't I see the path bar after I turn it on?
faq.answer: Click a file or folder in the window, or select a Favorites folder. A user in an Apple Community thread says the bar appears only when something is selected. Apple's page does not confirm this, but it is a quick thing to try.

faq.question: Does the path bar work in list view and column view?
faq.answer: iDownloadBlog says View > Show Path Bar shows the bar in all Finder windows, in any view mode. That article was first published in 2015 and shows a 2026 update, so compare its menu wording with your own screen.

faq.question: Can I copy a folder's path from the path bar?
faq.answer: Yes. Control-click the folder in the path bar to copy its pathname, as Apple's Mac Help page describes. Paste it into a note, an email, or a Terminal command.

faq.question: Is the Terminal command for the path bar safe to use?
faq.answer: It is unofficial. The command is defaults write com.apple.finder ShowPathbar -bool true, followed by killall Finder. Use the View menu first. macos-defaults.com lists Sonoma, Ventura, Monterey, and Big Sur, not Tahoe or macOS 27.

task: Show the path bar in Finder
appliesTo: Finder on Mac, with steps from Apple's macOS 27 Mac Help page
requirements: A Mac with Finder open, which every Mac has
A Finder window with a folder or file selected
About a minute of your time

steps.name: Open a Finder window
steps.text: Click the Finder icon in the Dock. If no Finder window is open, choose File > New Finder Window or press ⌘N. Select a folder in the sidebar so the window has something selected.
steps.tip: A user in an Apple Community thread says the bar appears when a Favorites folder or item is selected.

steps.name: Open the View menu
steps.text: With the Finder window active, click View in the menu bar at the top of the screen. The View menu holds the path bar and status bar options.
steps.tip: Make sure Finder is the frontmost app first, or the menu will show another app's items.

steps.name: Choose Show Path Bar
steps.text: Click Show Path Bar. The strip appears near the bottom of the window and lists the folders that contain the selected file or folder.
steps.tip: Apple's page gives the menu route only. The ⌥⌘P shortcut comes from third-party guides.

steps.name: Read the path bar
steps.text: Look at the bottom edge of the Finder window. Each name is a folder that holds the next name in the chain. The last item in the bar is the folder or file you selected.
steps.tip: If the bar shows only one name, select a folder inside another folder to see a longer chain.

steps.name: Move up with a click
steps.text: Click any folder in the path bar. Finder shows that folder's subfolders in the window, so you can find a sibling folder without going back.
steps.tip: Click the same name again later to return to the folder view you wanted.

steps.name: Copy a pathname
steps.text: Control-click a folder in the path bar. The menu lets you copy that folder's pathname, which you can paste into a note, an email, or a Terminal command.
steps.tip: Copying a path avoids typos in long folder chains.

steps.name: Hide the path bar
steps.text: Open View again and choose Show Path Bar. Mainspring says choosing it again hides the bar. Pressing ⌥⌘P a second time also toggles it.
steps.tip: If the shortcut does nothing, use the menu. Apple's page does not list the shortcut.

steps.name: Peek with the Option key
steps.text: Hold Option (⌥) while you look at the bottom of the Finder window. Apple describes the bar as shown momentarily, so it may hide again when you let go.
steps.tip: Use the peek when you only need to check a location, not for a permanent setting.

troubleshooting.problem: The path bar does not appear after I choose it.
troubleshooting.fix: Click a file or folder in the window, or select a Favorites folder. Then open View and check the setting again. A forum user says the bar shows only with a selection.

troubleshooting.problem: The View menu has no Show Path Bar item.
troubleshooting.fix: Make sure Finder is the active app, then click a Finder window and open View again. If the item still does not appear, check your version under Apple menu > About This Mac.
Apple's Mac Help page does not list this shortcut. Use View > Show Path Bar instead. Third-party guides can lag behind a new macOS version.
Check the exact spelling, including the capital P in ShowPathbar. Run defaults write com.apple.finder ShowPathbar -bool true, then killall Finder. If nothing changes, use the View menu.

troubleshooting.problem: I want the status bar but not the path bar.
troubleshooting.fix: Choose View > Show Status Bar or press ⌘/. Mainspring says the status bar appears at the bottom of the window when the path bar is off.
